clinicalPearls: Autosomal dominant multiple neoplasia and lentiginosis syndrome most commonly caused by germline inactivating variants in the PRKAR1A tumour-suppressor gene
Characteristic skin findings include spotty pigmentation (lentigines) with a typical distribution around the lips, eyes and genital region, and blue naevi
Cardiac myxomas can arise in any chamber and at multiple sites, carrying risk of embolism, obstruction and sudden death, and may recur after resection
Endocrine tumours include primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease causing ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome, and growth hormone-secreting pituitary tumours
Large-cell calcifying Sertoli cell tumours of the testis and thyroid nodules or tumours are recognised features
Psammomatous melanotic schwannoma is a distinctive associated tumour
PRKAR1A encodes a regulatory subunit of protein kinase A, so its loss increases cyclic-AMP-dependent signalling and drives tumour formation, particularly in endocrine tissues
reference.pathophysiology: Carney complex most often results from germline inactivating variants in PRKAR1A, which encodes the type 1-alpha regulatory subunit of protein kinase A. This subunit normally restrains the catalytic activity of protein kinase A; its loss leads to unregulated cyclic-AMP-dependent protein kinase A signalling. Overactive protein kinase A signalling promotes proliferation in hormonally responsive and other susceptible tissues, explaining the endocrine tumours, myxomas, pigmented skin lesions and schwannomas. Tumour development follows a tumour-suppressor mechanism with a somatic second hit. A minority of cases involve other loci, and some show genetic heterogeneity.
additionalDifferentials: McCune-Albright syndrome with endocrine hyperfunction and pigmentation
Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and other lentiginosis syndromes
Isolated Cushing syndrome from other adrenal or pituitary causes
additionalInvestigations: Germline molecular genetic testing of PRKAR1A including deletion/duplication analysis
Transthoracic echocardiography for cardiac myxomas, repeated on surveillance
Biochemical assessment for Cushing syndrome (including cortisol dynamics) and growth hormone/IGF-1 for acromegaly
Adrenal and pituitary imaging when endocrine hyperfunction is detected
Thyroid ultrasound and testicular ultrasound for characteristic tumours
Dermatological examination and documentation of lentigines and blue naevi
redFlags: Symptoms of embolism, syncope or heart failure suggesting a cardiac myxoma
Signs of Cushing syndrome from primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease
Recurrence of cardiac myxoma after previous surgical removal
New neurological deficit suggesting psammomatous melanotic schwannoma or embolic stroke
reference.prognosis: Cardiac myxomas are the leading cause of mortality through embolic events, obstruction and surgical risk, and can recur, so lifelong cardiac surveillance is essential. With regular monitoring and timely surgery for tumours, overall outlook is improved, though endocrine and other tumours require ongoing management.
pitfalls: Treating a cardiac myxoma as an isolated sporadic lesion and not screening for recurrence or the wider syndrome
Missing subtle spotty pigmentation that would point to the diagnosis
Overlooking ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome from primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease
Failing to arrange echocardiographic surveillance and genetic testing of relatives
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: Excise cardiac myxomas surgically, recognising that they may be multiple, arise in any chamber and recur after resection

Treat ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome from primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease, usually by bilateral adrenalectomy, and growth-hormone-secreting pituitary tumours by surgery with somatostatin analogues
Manage large-cell calcifying Sertoli cell tumours and thyroid tumours surgically as indicated
Undertake lifelong cardiac surveillance with regular echocardiography, given the dominant embolic and obstructive risk from myxomas
Provide ongoing biochemical and imaging surveillance for endocrine tumours
Coordinate multidisciplinary cardiac, endocrine and dermatological care
Offer PRKAR1A genetic testing, counselling and cascade screening of relatives, given autosomal dominant inheritance
